newsitem.title: USA: Colombian coffee output revised for 96-97 - attache.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee output revised for 96-97 - attache.

text.p: Colombian coffee production for marketing year 1996/97 (October/September) was revised downward to 10.3 million bags because of heavy rain, reduced prices, broca infestation and an increased age of coffee trees, a U.S. agricultural attache said in a report made public on Tuesday.
The report, dated June 15, also said Colombian coffee output for marketing year 1997-98 was forecast at 11.3 million bags.
Estimates of Colombia's coffee exports for 1996/97 were increased to 11 million bags, the report said.

"The increase in our export figure results from exceptionally high shipping volumes in recent months as the industry attempts to capitalize upon higher international prices and a strong demand from overseas buyers," the report said.
Coffee exports during 1977/98 were forecast to fall to 10.8 million bags due to a decline in exportable supplies, despite a projected 1 million bag increase in production because of low stocks.
The attache also lowered 1996/97 estimated ending stocks to 4.1 million bags, representing a 2.2 million bag decline in carryover stock levels compared to a year earlier.

"Despite the forecast million bag increase in coffee production in 1997/98, coffee supplies will be tight next year," the report said. "A further decline in coffee stocks to 3.1 million bags is forecast for September 30, 1998. Although low, this stock level does not pose a serious threat to the orderly marketing of Colombia's coffee."
